series: Things Living In Your House, Part 20
sources: UC Statewide IPM Program, Pest Notes: Termites: subterranean termites live in soil and reach wood through tunnels or shelter (mud) tubes made of saliva, soil and wood; drywood termites nest above ground and leave six-sided fecal pellets below exit holes; protists in the gut digest cellulose; colonies range up to hundreds of thousands, possibly millions; a 2,400 sq ft home can host several colonies; Reticulitermes swarm in spring or fall on clear days after heavy rain, most swarmers are eaten by predators; seeing swarms does not always mean the building is infested; damaged wood has a thin, easily punctured surface; inspect every 3-5 years; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/PESTNOTES/pn7415.html

University of Maryland Extension, Ants and Termites: How to Tell the Difference: ants have elbowed antennae, termites straight beaded ones; ants have a pinched waist, termites do not; ant front wings are longer than hind wings, termite wings are about equal in length; https://extension.umd.edu/resource/ants-and-termites-how-tell-difference

beats.say: Something is eating your house from the inside, and you can't see it.
One colony can grow to hundreds of thousands. Maybe millions.
Termites. Pale, soft workers that eat wood.
Tiny microbes in their gut turn the wood into food.
Underground termites build mud tubes up to the wood, to stay damp.
The wood looks fine outside. But it's thin, and a screwdriver pokes right through.
And one house can have several colonies at once.
Subscribe. Part twenty one is chewing tunnels in your walls.
